svg.text: The partograph: one page that tells you when to stop waiting
Cervical dilatation against time
ALERT
ACTION
Hours
this labour has
crossed the alert line
Plot in the active phase. Cross the alert line, reassess and prepare to move. Reach the action line, intervene.
What else goes on the same page
Foetal heart, half-hourly
Liquor: clear, meconium, blood, absent
Moulding: 0, +, ++, +++
Descent in fifths palpable above the brim
Contractions per ten minutes, and length
Oxytocin, drugs, fluids given
Pulse, blood pressure, temperature
Urine: volume, protein, acetone
Descent is recorded in fifths, not in centimetres.
Five fifths means completely above the brim.
Zero fifths means fully descended.
Moulding and the head that will not come
+++ moulding with the head still high, and a labour that has crossed the action line, is obstructed labour
until proved otherwise. Add a retraction ring, blood-stained urine or maternal exhaustion and it is an emergency.
Never augment with oxytocin when the problem may be obstruction. You will rupture the uterus.
Sutures touching is 0. Overlapped but reducible is ++. Overlapped and not reducible is +++.
A note on the 2020 WHO Labour Care Guide
WHO now defines the active first stage from 5 cm rather than 4 cm, replaces the alert and action lines with
time limits at each centimetre, and adds a second stage section. Many Ghanaian services still teach the
classic partograph, so know both — and know which one the chart in front of you actually is.
